title: From geometry to a testable photonic design
description: AIFIELD’s design workflow links layout and process descriptions to several forms of simulation. Each output answers a different engineering question and must be interpreted within its model assumptions.
lead: AIFIELD’s design workflow links layout and process descriptions to several forms of simulation. Each output answers a different engineering question and must be interpreted within its model assumptions.

sections.heading: Design inputs
body: An engineer defines geometry, layers, materials and process constraints. Those inputs set the context for simulations; incomplete fabrication assumptions can make an attractive simulated layout unsuitable for a real process.

sections.heading: Simulation views
body: Mode analysis examines guided light in a structure; circuit models connect components; field calculations show spatial behavior; thermal analysis examines heating effects. The September 2026 description presents this range of work, while exact support and validated accuracy need current confirmation.

sections.heading: A glucose-chip design example
body: The internal photonic glucose example shows how a sensing question can guide component design and simulation. It is an engineering design output, not a fabricated chip measurement. Fabrication tolerances and measured agreement are separate validation steps.
